cells.tense: A shape is forming in front of you and you are letting it stay unfinished.
cells.act: hold the cloud of possible feeling without picking yet
cells.ask: Let a shape you've spotted stay open this week — name every version of it to yourself and pick none.
cells.core:
You can hold a shape without setting it, and that holding is its own kind of seeing. What you notice about how something is turning stays in your hands as possibility longer than most people can stand; it doesn't rush you into a forecast. That's the same faculty doing what it does best — reading the pattern without turning it into a verdict, letting what might be felt have room before you name it.

Let a shape you've spotted stay open this week. Name every version to yourself and pick none of them. The pull of what might come is worth following a little way before you close it. Staying with the unfinished shape is not hesitation — it's the part of the work that only happens before the call.
cells.sheetLine: You can see it and not call it, for now.
cells.verb: Reading the shape before it finishes arriving
cells.place: Where what you are becomes what you become

cells.tense: You are already speaking the ending of a pattern still in the middle of arriving.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Choose a kept-level thing you've been carrying a long time, move on it today, and skip the preamble.
cells.core:
When the reading runs fast, you forecast the next move and say it with such certainty that the room reorganizes around what hasn't happened yet. The shape gets delivered early, by you, and the thing still unfolding starts bending toward the version you announced. Being what you are doesn't need the conclusion declared; it needs your hands working while the thing is still wet.

Choose a kept-level thing you've been carrying a long time, move on it today, and skip the preamble. Acting inside the moment is how this part remembers what it is. You'll spend the afternoon catching up to what you just did — that's what it is to be the one who moved, not the one who forecast.
cells.sheetLine: You are already writing an ending for something still opening.
cells.verb: Reading the shape before it finishes arriving
cells.place: Where what you are becomes what you become

cells.tense: Something has been showing itself to you and you keep looking past it.
cells.act: go deeper into the shared thing than comfort allows
cells.ask: In a conversation you'd normally keep light, stay long past the practical exchange and say the piece you'd edit out.
cells.core:
Note: none. A shape keeps presenting itself and you keep walking by the place where you could say it. What you've been turning over stays unnamed, and a thing you understood doesn't get to become a shared one. That's the door you're at — not one you missed, one you're standing in front of.

In a conversation you'd normally keep light, stay long past the practical exchange and say the piece you'd edit out. That's not solving anything; it's what the reading is for. What you've been keeping to yourself gets said across to someone, and comes back as something alive instead of a pile of notes.

cells.tense: The shape is on the table and someone else has been handed credit for reading it.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: Go once toward the pull you keep circling — not to decide it or claim it, just stand close and look.
cells.core:
You watch something move, make the call without noticing you made it, and wait to be told what you saw — the recognition filed as someone else's, as luck, as the room. Meanwhile the pattern you've been reading about what your own life is becoming has been read by you the whole time. The credit you're waiting for is one you haven't handed back to yourself.

Move once toward the pull you keep circling — not to decide it or claim it, just close enough to see. Following the pull is the same attention you already give everything else, aimed at what's next. You'll find your own reading in the margin, in your own hand.
cells.sheetLine: The pattern you keep seeing is the one you keep writing off.
cells.verb: Reading the shape before it finishes arriving
cells.place: Where what you are becomes what you become
